title: Horsehead Nebula found on a Harvard plate
summary: Fleming, a founding member of the Harvard Computers who led the Draper Catalogue work, catalogued over ten thousand stars and discovered the Horsehead Nebula on a photographic plate in 1888.
why: One of the sky's most famous objects, found by a plate reader.

notes.problem: Source does not call her 'head of Harvard's women computers'; it says 'one of the founding members' and in charge of the Draper Catalogue.

unsung.contribution: Identified the Horsehead Nebula and catalogued thousands of stars for the Harvard spectral survey.
unsung.recognition: The first Dreyer Index Catalogue left her name out, attributing the Harvard discoveries to Pickering.
